title: Medical information drafts with an evidence trail
summary: A controlled assistant that drafts responses from approved materials for medical-information specialists to review.
goals: Reduce specialist time spent assembling routine response drafts.
Keep every factual claim linked to current approved content.
Demonstrate a safe workflow for escalation and human approval.
inScope: One agreed product/topic set using a versioned approved-content snapshot.
Draft replies with citations and explicit insufficient-evidence handling.
A reviewer queue using synthetic or approved de-identified queries.
A specialist-led evaluation of accuracy, coverage and escalation.
outOfScope: Direct replies to HCPs or autonomous medical advice.
New scientific claims or content approval by the assistant.
Production mailbox integration and pharmacovigilance automation.
Full product-portfolio coverage or external publication.

assumptions.text: The medical-information owner can supply current approved documents.
Specialists will review every draft before any use.
A limited-topic pilot can be evaluated without live mailbox access.

questions.question: Which topic generates enough repeat demand to justify a pilot?
questions.why: Concentrates the pilot on a credible value case.

questions.question: How are approved content versions and expiry dates represented?
questions.why: Prevents superseded documents entering a response.

questions.question: What is the existing adverse-event and off-label escalation procedure?
questions.why: The assistant must defer to an established specialist workflow.

questions.question: Who approves intended use, evidence handling and pilot evaluation?
questions.why: Makes the compliance gate explicit before any build.

phases.name: Discover
phases.objective: Define the topic boundary, approved-content snapshot and compliance gate.
activities: Interview the sponsor and nominated pilot users.
Profile approved sample data and identify access gaps.
Agree baseline measures, acceptance thresholds and a go/no-go gate.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor signs off the pilot boundary, data access and evaluation plan.

phases.name: Design
phases.objective: Turn agreed outcomes and controls into a buildable pilot design.
activities: Map the bounded workflow and reviewer responsibilities.
Define interfaces, failure handling and evidence requirements.
Review the design with the operational and compliance owners.
phases.exitCriteria: Design and required control owners approve the implementation plan.

phases.name: Build
phases.objective: Implement evidence-linked drafting, abstention and specialist review.
activities: Implement only the agreed data inputs and workflow.
Add traceability, access controls and explicit failure states.
Evaluate representative and adversarial cases against the reference set.
phases.exitCriteria: The test cohort meets agreed quality thresholds; critical issues are resolved.

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective: Evaluate usefulness and reliability with the agreed user cohort.
activities: Onboard pilot users and train reviewers.
Run a bounded trial against the baseline.
Capture errors, review effort and user feedback.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor reviews measured results and decides to stop, iterate or expand.

phases.name: Handover
phases.objective: Give the owner a controlled, maintainable next step.
activities: Document the workflow, limits and operational runbook.
Present the pilot findings and a separately scoped rollout option.
phases.exitCriteria: Named owner accepts the handover and the next-step decision is recorded.

drivers.detail: Content currency, version metadata and topic coverage need checking.
Medical-information review and controlled intended-use approval.
All response drafts require specialist review.

risks.risk: Unsupported claims appear in otherwise plausible drafts.
risks.mitigation: Require claim-level evidence and abstention; score unsupported claims separately.
Only index an approved versioned snapshot; exclude expired materials.
Agree a limited shadow pilot; do not connect a live sending channel.

metrics.target: Proposed: zero unsupported factual claims in the agreed evaluation set.
Proposed: 30% reduction against a specialist baseline.
Proposed: 100% of seeded escalation cases routed for manual review.
